_note: Vetted static hints, keyed by recall item id. Used when the student has not agreed to AI processing, when the model is unavailable, and in tests. A hint must never contain the answer.

eit-1.title: Nudge
eit-1.text: Think about how many parts of the system each test touches at once.

eit-1.title: Concept
eit-1.text: A unit test checks one component in isolation, often with fake versions of the parts it depends on. An integration test checks that two or more real components work together through the interface between them.

eit-1.title: Worked example
eit-1.text: Think of a bicycle. Squeezing the brake lever to see that it moves is like a unit test. Squeezing it and checking that the wheel actually slows down is like an integration test: the lever, cable and brake pad all have to work together.

eit-2.title: Nudge
eit-2.text: Think about what you can do when a part you depend on is not ready yet.

eit-2.title: Concept
eit-2.text: One way to keep testing is to put a fake in the missing part's place. The fake only returns fixed replies, but that is enough for the part above it to run.

eit-2.title: Worked example
eit-2.text: Imagine rehearsing a play before the lead actor arrives. A helper reads the lead's lines from a script so the other actors can practise their cues. The scene runs, even though the real actor is missing.

uta-1.title: Nudge
uta-1.text: Think about which tests you would have to repeat again and again.

uta-1.title: Concept
uta-1.text: Machines are good at doing the same steps exactly the same way many times. People are good at noticing that something feels wrong.

uta-1.title: Worked example
uta-1.text: A washing machine handles the weekly laundry, but you still check by eye whether a new shirt's colour will run.

uta-2.title: Nudge
uta-2.text: Ask what is different between your laptop and the build server, especially speed.

uta-2.title: Concept
uta-2.text: Tests that depend on how fast something loads, or on data another test left behind, can pass or fail by chance.

uta-2.title: Worked example
uta-2.text: It is like texting a friend 'I'm here' before checking they've opened the door: sometimes they have, sometimes not.

uta-3.title: Nudge
uta-3.text: Think about when a broken change is found, and by whom.

uta-3.title: Concept
uta-3.text: Running checks automatically at the moment code is shared means problems surface while the change is still small and fresh.

uta-3.title: Worked example
uta-3.text: A smoke alarm that sounds as soon as the toast burns is more useful than finding the smoke damage next week.

rtf-1.title: Nudge
rtf-1.text: Imagine the developer reading your report has never seen the bug happen.

rtf-1.title: Concept
rtf-1.text: A report has to let someone else see the same problem and know what should have happened instead.

rtf-1.title: Worked example
rtf-1.text: A recipe that says 'make the cake' is useless; one with ingredients, steps and a photo of the result can be followed.

rtf-2.title: Nudge
rtf-2.text: One of these is about damage, the other is about timing.

rtf-2.title: Concept
rtf-2.text: How much a problem hurts the system and how urgently the business needs it fixed are separate questions with separate answers.

rtf-2.title: Worked example
rtf-2.text: A small stain on a wedding dress the night before the wedding is minor damage but very urgent.

rtf-3.title: Nudge
rtf-3.text: Think about the one decision the reader of the summary has to make.

rtf-3.title: Concept
rtf-3.text: A summary gives the overall picture, the biggest risks, and a recommendation, rather than every detail.

rtf-3.title: Worked example
rtf-3.text: A weather forecast says 'bring an umbrella', not every pressure reading taken that day.
